flags.text: We read AGENTS.md, README.md, knowledge/INDEX.md, knowledge/DATA.md, LOCAL_STORAGE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, the registry, the editorial rules, redistribution rules, REUSE.md and LICENSE. The October 11 settlement prospection retrospective identified geographic and chronological joins as recurring failure points. The October 24 town-axis register preserves site phases but does not compare them with modern civic settlement. The October 25 continuity package distinguishes practical inheritance from a demonstrated lineage. We will add an explicit modern-place-to-excavated-place relation, evidence dates and continuity claims with their source scope.

The validator will check required fields, unique IDs, source references, geographic bounds, date intervals, period overlap logic, explicit source scope, and the absence of a verified continuity claim without supporting sequence evidence. We will review the prose and run the knowledge checks. No reading, sign key, meaning map, restoration, segmentation or script conjecture is submitted, so no bench scorer measures this endpoint. We read bench/README.md; its five scientific tasks do not evaluate a settlement source register. No confirmation half or spent statistic family will be opened.

The knowledge check passes with no errors or warnings, leaving the two expected generated-file maintainer notes. The repository integrity snapshot reports sixty errors, all outside this contribution, including the existing distributed-path check for data/MANIFEST.json. The prose review's generic citation label was corrected. Its two remaining flags are repository path strings in the frozen protocol and are retained. The checks and their command output are preserved in checks-v1.json and checks-v2.json. No statistical benchmark evaluates this metadata review; no script reading or new historical conjecture was submitted, and no confirmation data were opened.

We start from the town-axis visual atlas, the Q-1032 town-axis register and the shared-infrastructure plan study of 24 October 2026. They retain published plans, orientation conflicts, dimensions and phase limitations. Their source images remain local. The new work adds procedural metric geometry, interactive inspection and export; it does not rerun their archaeological comparisons. We will verify factual building dimensions against excavator publications and official archaeological or UNESCO records. New source witnesses go under physical `D:/projects/indus_valley_script/data/raw/2026-10-26-indus-living-atlas/reconstruction/`, reachable at logical `data/raw/2026-10-26-indus-living-atlas/reconstruction/`.
